Alright, the user just expressed frustration: “why is part of it being filled in? thats not our logo anymore. Why did it turn black? I said make it look better, not change our logo.” They want the logo to remain an outline, not filled, and definitely not turning black. In the previous edits I already stripped the fill animation and set fill to transparent, removed the fill‑in keyframes from the `.ai-fill-source-202606` rule, and eliminated the `animation: aiLogoFillIn202606 …` line. That should have prevented any fill from appearing.

However, there may still be residual behavior that causes the logo to appear black or filled in under certain conditions. Looking at the CSS, I see that the `@keyframes aiLogoFillIn202606` and `@keyframes aiLogoStrokeOut202606` are still defined, and the reduced‑motion media query still forces the `.ai-fill-source-202606` element to have `opacity:1;` (which would make any fill visible). Even though I removed the fill animation from the main rule, the reduced‑motion block still overrides it and forces the fill source to be fully opaque, which could result in a black fill showing up when the user has reduced‑motion enabled or when the media query is applied for any reason.

Since the user wants the logo to stay outline‑only under all circumstances, I need to ensure that the reduced‑motion fallback also respects the outline‑only design. The simplest way is to delete the `.ai-fill-source-202606` rule inside the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block, or at least set its opacity to 0 (or remove the rule entirely). Additionally, the `@keyframes aiLogoFillIn202606` and `@keyframes aiStrokeOut202606` are now unnecessary because we are no longer using any fill or stroke‑out animations. Removing them cleans up the CSS and eliminates any chance of unintended effects.

But I also need to be careful not to break the draw animation for the stroke segments. The reduced‑motion block currently disables animations on the draw segments and also forces `opacity:0!important;` on them, which is fine. However, it also sets `stroke-dasharray` to its default via `animation:none;opacity:0!important;`. To keep the outline visible even when animations are disabled, I should replace the `opacity:0!important;` with a proper static stroke‑dasharray that shows the full path, ensuring the logo still appears as an outline. So I will modify the `.ai-draw-segment-202606` rule inside the reduced‑motion block to set `stroke-dasharray:var(--segment-length) var(--path-length);` and remove the `opacity:0!important;`. This will make the segments visible as a complete outline when animations are disabled, matching the desired “outline only” look.

Putting this together, the edit I need to make is to replace the entire block that currently contains the fill‑source rule and the keyframes with a slimmer version that only disables animations on the SVG and draw segments, and ensures the draw segments are rendered with the full dasharray. I will therefore target the exact string that includes the keyframes and the reduced‑motion block, and replace it with a new reduced‑motion block that omits the fill‑source rule and updates the draw‑segment rule accordingly.

Thus, the precise edit is:
- `old_string`: the block from `@keyframes aiLogoFillIn202606{...}` through the end of the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){...}` including the fill‑source rule.
- `new_string`: a reduced‑motion block that only contains the SVG, ::after, and draw‑segment rules, with the draw‑segment rule setting `stroke-dasharray:var(--segment-length) var(--path-length);` and no opacity overrides.

This aligns with the user’s request to keep the logo as an outline and prevents any black fill from appearing, while still respecting reduced‑motion preferences. I will now issue the Edit tool call with these parameters.
